analysis.investment_thesis: CapitalNumbers screens well on the Magic Formula: earnings yield of ~15% (EBIT 30 Cr / EV ~203 Cr, likely higher adjusting for post-IPO cash) paired with ROCE of 26.5% and zero debt. Cheap AND good — exactly the combination the formula seeks, though small-cap IT services cyclicality warrants position sizing discipline.
key_strengths: Earnings Yield ~15% (EBIT 30 Cr / MC 203 Cr) — attractive per Magic Formula threshold >12%
ROCE 26.5% and ROE 20% — capital-efficient, asset-light IT services model
Debt-free balance sheet, 5/5 years positive OCF, 39% PAT CAGR over 5 years
key_risks: FY25 EBIT dipped from 34→30 Cr — watch for margin compression / growth deceleration
Small-cap IT services exposure: client concentration and currency/discretionary-spend cyclicality
77 Cr investing outflow in FY25 — capital deployment execution risk on recently raised funds
red_flags: Operating income and OCF both declined YoY in FY25 despite revenue growth — early sign of operating leverage reversing
analysis.detailed_analysis: Running the Magic Formula: Earnings Yield = EBIT/EV = 30 / ~203 ≈ 14.8% (likely 18%+ adjusted for net cash from the FY25 equity raise of 64 Cr financing inflow, since borrowings are zero and equity jumped from 67→171 Cr). Return on Capital is excellent — reported ROCE 26.5%, which comfortably clears my >20% bar, and the capital base is light (no CWIP, minimal fixed assets for a services firm). Both factors rank well — this is the rare combo of cheap AND good that the formula is designed to surface. P/E of 8.91 against 39% 5Y PAT CAGR is statistically mispriced on its face.\n\nThe caveats keep this from an 8+: FY25 showed the first signs of deceleration — Operating Income contracted 34→30 Cr, OCF fell 22→19 Cr, and revenue growth slowed to ~2% YoY (98→100 Cr). If FY26 confirms a plateau rather than a dip, the earnings yield compresses. The 77 Cr investing outflow funded by the IPO raise is also a watch item — capital allocation on fresh cash is where high-ROIC stories often go wrong. Still, on a systematic basis, this is a buy-the-basket candidate: cheap on EBIT/EV, high on ROC, debt-free, 74.67% promoter skin-in-the-game. I'd size it as one of many in a Magic Formula portfolio rather than concentrate.
